I don’t have real‑time data built into this chat, so I can’t tell you the exact Air Quality Index (AQI) for Los Angeles at this moment. However, you can quickly check the current conditions on a few reliable sources:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and you’ll see the latest AQI, pollutant breakdown, and health advisories. |
| **BreezoMeter** | Go to https://www.breezometer.com/, search for Los Angeles, and you’ll get a live AQI, forecast, and alerts. |
| **Weather.com** | Search “Los Angeles AQI” on the weather site; it shows the current AQI and a short forecast. |
| **Mobile Apps** | Apps like “AirVisual” or “Plume Labs: Air Report” provide real‑time AQI and health recommendations. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot right now, you can also try a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask, “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They pull from the same data feeds.

Let me know if you’d like a quick summary of what the AQI categories mean or how to interpret the numbers!
